paper.title_en: The $w$-mode instability of strangeon ergostars and its impact on energy extraction
paper.abstract_en: Rapidly rotating compact ergostars have been proposed as alternative central engines for short gamma-ray bursts. However, competing energy-loss channels, such as gravitational-wave emission driven by non-axisymmetric instabilities, could curtail the power available for relativistic electromagnetic outflows. In this work, we investigate the $w$-mode instability of rapidly rotating strangeon ergostars by solving the coupled spacetime and fluid perturbation equations in the Hilbert gauge using a spectral method, without relying on a slow-rotation approximation. We calculate the complex eigenvalues of the axial-led and polar-led $w$-mode branches originating from the fundamental $l=m=2$ modes of nonrotating stars along the maximum-energy-extraction paths of twelve representative strangeon equations of state. We find that both branches remain damped throughout these paths, despite the presence of ergoregions. We further vary the stellar angular velocity to determine the instability thresholds. In every case with an identified threshold, the angular velocity at the corresponding extraction-path endpoint remains below the critical value, with the largest ratio being $0.926$. Our results indicate that the $w$-mode instabilities examined here do not provide a growing gravitational-wave emission channel along the considered energy-extraction paths, supporting the availability of the previously estimated rotational energy reservoirs for electromagnetic extraction.
